events.title: Washington Elected First U.S. President
events.description: The U.S. Electoral College met and unanimously chose George Washington as the first President of the United States. He received every electoral vote cast.
events.significance: Washington's unanimous election gave the new federal government early legitimacy. His conduct in office set precedents that later presidents followed.

events.title: France Abolishes Slavery
events.description: The French revolutionary legislature, the National Convention, voted to abolish slavery throughout all French territories. The decree applied to colonies such as Saint-Domingue.
events.significance: It was one of the first abolitions of slavery by a major colonial power. Napoleon reinstated slavery in 1802, so the abolition did not last.

events.title: Birth of Rosa Parks
events.description: Rosa Louise McCauley was born in Tuskegee, Alabama. She later became known by her married name, Rosa Parks.
events.significance: Parks' refusal to give up her bus seat in 1955 helped spark the Montgomery Bus Boycott. She became one of the best-known figures of the American civil rights movement.

events.title: Yalta Conference Opens
events.description: Winston Churchill, Franklin D. Roosevelt and Joseph Stalin met at the Livadia Palace in Crimea. They discussed how to end World War II and how to reorganize postwar Europe.
events.significance: The agreements reached at Yalta shaped the postwar order in Europe. They also became a source of Cold War controversy over the division of the continent.

events.title: Facebook Launches
events.description: Harvard sophomore Mark Zuckerberg launched a social network called TheFacebook from his dorm room. It was initially open only to Harvard students.
events.significance: It grew into one of the world's largest social platforms, with billions of users. It changed how people communicate, share news and organize socially.
